_comment: Coverage matrix for the shared Carve spec corpus (spec/tests/corpus/*.crv). Every NN-slug base category must appear in covered or skip; the coverage-matrix test fails otherwise so a new spec category forces a classify decision. covered = grammar parses every file in the category with no ERROR/MISSING node. skip = at least one file currently produces an ERROR/MISSING node; reason records the unmodeled construct (a grammar gap to surface, not to hack around). A skip key is a CATEGORY (NN-slug) or a single EXAMPLE (NN-slug-2) — use the example form when the rest of the category parses cleanly, so one gap does not drop assertion for its siblings. A key equal to a category name is read as the CATEGORY, so the first example of a category cannot be skipped on its own. REASONS: a ledger entry's `reason` may be `ref:<key>`, resolving against the top-level `reasons` map, so one grammar gap spanning a whole category states its explanation once. coverage-matrix gates it both ways - a ref with no entry fails, and a reasons entry nothing references fails, because a reason nobody points at is an excuse that outlived the gap it excused.

a-trailing-comment-takes-a-tab-a-run-sta.reason: a caption whose text is only a comment is no caption: the `^` stays paragraph text after the image. The grammar does not see that the comment empties the caption line.

an-unclosed-backtick-run-still-forms-mat.reason: the unclosed backtick run after `$$` still forms empty display math, which renders inside a paragraph; the grammar builds the math node the engine builds, so only the block check differs.

citation-shaped-lines-remain-core-text-2.reason: a citation-shaped line is core text in the next carve release; the grammar still reads it as a citation definition.

a-caption-host-and-a-continuation-cell-r.reason: an image followed by an inline comment is not a whole-paragraph image, so the `^` line is paragraph text; the same host check as a-caret-line-does-not-end-a-paragraph-it-cannot-caption.

an-unterminated-raw-fence-keeps-literal-.reason: a raw block for a non-HTML format renders nothing, so the expected HTML is the paragraph alone; the engine's AST builds the raw_block the grammar builds.

an-all-blank-raw-payload-still-emits-its.reason: the source deliberately opens a raw block whose payload is one blank line. Its expected HTML is therefore only a newline, which has no HTML element for the comparison pass to count; the raw_block node is the correct source structure rather than a grammar error.

a-caret-line-does-not-end-a-paragraph-it.reason: a caret line after ordinary prose is paragraph text, but the context-free grammar cannot make caption recognition depend on whether the preceding block is one of the five captionable hosts, so it builds a caption node here. The renderer/parser implementations apply the host check and keep the line literal.

an-unresolved-image-gives-its-whole-capt.reason: the same host check as a-caret-line-does-not-end-a-paragraph-it-cannot-caption, reached by the one host whose captionability is not decidable from the line at all. `![a][r]` / `^ cap one` is a captionable IMAGE only if `[r]` resolves, and whether it resolves is a fact about the whole document. Measured against this category's own -2, which is byte-identical for the first three lines and adds `[r]: /u` five lines down: the grammar builds the same caption node in both, so the caption here is not a defect in the caret rule but the reference resolution a context-free grammar has no access to. The renderer resolves the reference first and keeps this line literal, which is why the expected HTML is one paragraph.

a-caret-line-does-not-end-a-paragraph-it.reason: a paragraph that merely contains an image is not a captionable host; deciding that the image is the paragraph's whole content needs semantic context beyond this grammar's local caret-line rule, so it over-accepts the caret line as a caption.

an-unresolved-reference-image-takes-no-c.reason: `![a][nope]` + `^ cap` is one paragraph: the reference does not resolve, so the image is literal text and the `^` line is literal with it. Whether it resolves depends on the DEFINITIONS in the document, which a context-free grammar does not have - so the caption is built here and cannot be declined without a symbol table. The renderer decides correctly; highlighting a caption that the language declines is the cost.
